summary.note: 2026-10-07: no prior forecast resolved this cycle (the fc-2026-09-09-parnell-nomination window closes ~10/9, two days out, and remains PENDING with a note added reflecting Sen. Cramer's public objection). Four new PENDING forecasts added: whether the shutdown materially delays a Golden Dome program milestone within 30 days; whether the Houthi-Yemeni-government front produces a further cross-front engagement within 14 days; whether the 10/6-10/7 Ukraine mass strike produces a concrete new Western response within 14 days; and whether the Parnell Army Secretary nomination is withdrawn or its window lapses without a transmittal within 14 days.

forecasts.forecast: The CMMC 60-day review will conclude with a reformed-but-intact program and a reset phased timeline (not a repeal).
forecasts.note: The Task Force report remains non-public past its cited ~28 Sep target. Confirmed the Task Force convened in early Sept to review 1,100+ RFI comments; the ~100 authorized C3PAOs against >100,000 companies needing assessment remains an arithmetic constraint supporting the reformed-but-intact base case.

forecasts.forecast: Golden Dome award tempo will accelerate through late 2026 into early 2027.
forecasts.note: No new SDA/MDA award this cycle. The 29 Sep SASC hearing (CSIS's Karako, CBO's Mosher as witnesses) and 30 Sep SDA Transport Layer A launch are now imminent and will be the next direct tests of this forecast; the unresolved ~$185B-versus-~$1.2T cost divergence remains the main risk to the acceleration thesis.

forecasts.forecast: The Kyiv-Moscow long-range-strike pause will lapse at term absent a broader framework.
forecasts.note: Rather than a simple lapse, a 7 Sep Trump-Putin call produced a different, narrower, category-bounded 30-day energy-infrastructure strike-halt commitment (contingent on Ukrainian reciprocity) - neither a clean lapse nor a comprehensive framework. The capital-strike pause itself subsequently lapsed cleanly on 8 Sep with a mass resumed attack on Kyiv, confirming the base-case half of this forecast.

forecasts.forecast: China will not materially relax rare-earth/magnet controls on military-affiliated firms in the near term.
forecasts.note: Confirmed and extended: June 2026 entity-list action specifically targets MP Materials and USA Rare Earth, showing continued tightening rather than relaxation. No new PRC action through 9 Sep continues to support this.

forecasts.forecast: Iran will follow through on its threatened 'faster, heavier, more painful' response with at least one further strike on a U.S.-linked or U.S.-flagged vessel or asset within 30 days.
forecasts.note: The IRGC claimed strikes on two U.S. Navy destroyers and multiple tankers on 8 Sep, matching the threat's target selection and tone, but CENTCOM says the attempts failed and no U.S. vessel was hit -- the attempt is confirmed, the outcome (a successful strike) is not.

forecasts.forecast: The reported 30-day Ukraine energy-infrastructure strike-halt commitment will not hold cleanly for its full term without at least one contested violation claim from either side.
forecasts.note: Trump publicly claimed on 14 Sep that a mutual halt was in effect; Zelensky disputed the characterization as merely 'a proposal for a mutual halt'; Ukraine continued striking Russian refining infrastructure (the TANECO refinery, 13-14 Sep) amid a record U.S. diesel price -- a clear contested-violation-claim scenario, resolved well within the 30-day window. Tracked on the Ukraine Ceasefire Diplomacy / Zaporizhzhia thread.

forecasts.forecast: External power will be restored to the Zaporizhzhia plant (or sufficient diesel resupply will occur) before onsite fuel is exhausted, avoiding a station blackout.
forecasts.note: External power was restored 7 Sep 19:02 local via the repaired Ferrosplavna-1 line, well within the fuel window; the IAEA-brokered local ceasefire held long enough to complete the repair. Power status unchanged as of 9 Sep.

forecasts.forecast: The DoW CIO's internal CMMC Reform Task Force determination (~13 Sep) will recommend resuming assessment scaling on a revised timeline rather than a further indefinite pause or repeal.
forecasts.note: The 14-day horizon has now lapsed without any public output against which to grade. Deliberately not forced to a resolution: the determination's content remains non-public and grading it either way would be fabrication. Re-anchored to the cited ~28 Sep public-report date. Tracked on the CMMC Implementation thread.

forecasts.forecast: Iran will formally publish and attempt to enforce the Hormuz-adjacent 'exclusion zone,' but will not succeed in materially reducing U.S.-escorted commercial transit volumes within 30 days.
forecasts.note: Graded early on substance. The first clause is unmet: no formal exclusion-zone publication has been identified, though enforcement activity is evident. The second clause is now contradicted -- reporting this cycle describes Iran's blockade as having cut off most Gulf oil exports from global markets, with U.S. diesel at a record above $6.50/gal, which is material reduction in commercial transit even if the specific U.S.-escorted subset remains unquantified. Trending toward INCORRECT. Tracked on the U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz thread.

forecasts.forecast: CISA will add the MikroTik RouterOS 'MikroTrick' CVEs (2026-67276 / 2026-86060) to the KEV catalog within 30 days given confirmed active exploitation.
forecasts.note: CISA added CVE-2026-67277 (the correct identifier for the missing-authentication CVE, superseding the earlier-cited 2026-67276) and CVE-2026-86060 to KEV on 10 Sep 2026, well within the 30-day window and closing an 8-day disclosure-to-listing gap. Tracked on the Actively Exploited Edge / AI-Infra / Windows CVEs thread.

forecasts.forecast: DoD will proceed with removing Anthropic's models from GenAI.mil by late September as stated, absent a D.C. Circuit stay or injunction.
forecasts.note: No D.C. Circuit ruling and no new migration reporting across the gap. The 29 Sep department-wide removal deadline is now eight days out and resolves this forecast either way. Tracked on the DoD AI Vendor Governance / Anthropic Dispute thread.

forecasts.forecast: Iran will conduct at least one further attempted kinetic strike (successful or not) against a U.S. or U.S.-linked vessel within 14 days, continuing the claim/denial pattern established 8 Sep.
forecasts.note: The 11 Sep IRGC claim of a strike on a US Saildrone-type UUV, plus UKMTO's report of projectiles hitting two vessels off Oman, constitute a further attempted strike well within the 14-day window (resolved in 2 days). CENTCOM had not confirmed or denied the UUV claim as of this brief. Tracked on the U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz thread.

forecasts.forecast: The narrower Ukraine energy-infrastructure-specific strike halt (separate from the already-lapsed capital-strike pause) will be explicitly confirmed violated by a specific power-grid-targeted strike within 14 days.
forecasts.note: Ukraine's 19-20 Sep strike package -- its largest of the war -- damaged a facility at the Moscow oil refinery, an unambiguous energy-infrastructure strike inside the 14-day window. But refining is not the power grid and no grid-targeted strike was confirmed, so the forecast's specific test was not met. The deeper flaw is in the framing: no mutually agreed halt ever existed to be violated -- Zelensky described a proposal and Russia never accepted it. Directionally right, imprecisely specified. Tracked on the Ukraine Ceasefire Diplomacy / Zaporizhzhia thread.

forecasts.forecast: Trump will formally nominate a permanent Army Secretary (Parnell or otherwise) within 30 days.
forecasts.note: No formal nomination; Adam Telle continues as acting Secretary. Sen. Kevin Cramer (R-ND) publicly called the Parnell pick 'a bridge too far' over 2021 domestic-violence allegations -- the most explicit GOP objection to date. As of 10/7, still no transmittal found; window closes ~10/9, now two days out. Tracked on the DoD Leadership Continuity thread.

forecasts.forecast: A methodologically transparent third-party report (e.g., Lloyd's List Intelligence, Kpler, or S&P Global Commodity Insights) will publish a verified Hormuz transit-volume figure within 14 days that reconciles the conflicting 'effectively closed' (war-risk-insurance-based) and '~10 ships/day' (shipping-data-based) characterizations currently in circulation.
forecasts.note: Kpler (10-day average ~13/day) and Lloyd's List Intelligence (~12/day, 26 Aug-1 Sep) converge closely with each other on day 1 of the window, meaningfully narrowing the range — but a lower single-day operational figure (7 transits on 9 Sep) and the war-risk-insurance-based 'effectively closed' framing remain unreconciled with the AIS-tracker consensus, so this is a partial rather than full reconciliation. Tracked on the U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz thread.

forecasts.forecast: Given the 9 Sep KEV additions of Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway (CVE-2026-19490) and Cisco Firewall Management Center (CVE-2026-20079) authentication-bypass flaws, at least one confirmed enterprise or DIB-sector intrusion attribution involving one of these two CVEs will be publicly reported within 30 days.
forecasts.note: Cisco Talos publicly attributed active FMC exploitation to three clusters, including one assessed high-confidence to overlap with Russian GRU-linked Sandworm tooling and one assessed high-confidence as a Qilin ransomware affiliate — well within the 30-day window. Tracked on the Actively Exploited Edge / DevOps / AI-Infra CVEs thread.

forecasts.forecast: The Navy will not resume regular fleet operations at Naval Support Activity Bahrain within 90 days, instead continuing reliance on Diego Garcia-centric and afloat/dispersed Gulf basing.
forecasts.note: No new reconstruction-timeline or basing announcement identified across the gap. The 19 Sep Houthi strike on Riyadh argues against near-term normalization of fixed Gulf basing. Window has roughly nine weeks remaining.

forecasts.forecast: The 14 Sep Salalah, Oman ministerial meeting between GCC states and Iran will produce a temporary, informal Hormuz shipping arrangement but not a comprehensive US-Iran ceasefire.
forecasts.note: The meeting was postponed entirely rather than held — it produced no arrangement of any kind, informal or otherwise. A narrower bilateral Iran-Oman shipping-lane track and a newly opened Iran-UAE channel (BRICS summit, 13 Sep) continue separately. Tracked on the U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz thread.

forecasts.forecast: The reported fire/thermal activity along Saudi Arabia's East-West 'Petroline' pipeline (10 Sep) will NOT be confirmed by Saudi Aramco/government or independent reporting as an attack, consistent with the thermal signature's correspondence to known flare sites.
forecasts.note: Multiple outlets (Al Jazeera, CNN) confirmed a real multi-drone attack from Iraqi territory on 10-11 Sep, and CNBC published satellite imagery on 14 Sep confirming the damage; Saudi Arabia shut the pipeline. Attribution remains unclaimed/UNKNOWN. Tracked on the U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz thread.

forecasts.forecast: Saudi Arabia will restore East-West Petroline pipeline flow within 30 days, but attribution for the 10-11 Sep strike will remain unclaimed/unresolved within that window.
forecasts.note: Partial flow restoration was achieved well within 30 days (satisfying the 'restore flow' clause) and attribution for the 10-11 Sep strike remains unclaimed (satisfying the second clause), but reported capacity figures conflict across sources (recent reporting of ~2.2M bpd / ~40% of a ~5.5M bpd baseline vs. earlier reporting of ~4M bpd / ~57% of a 7M bpd nameplate) and full restoration remains outstanding, so this is graded PARTIAL rather than CORRECT pending reconciliation. Tracked on the U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz thread.

forecasts.forecast: A rescheduled GCC-Iran ministerial meeting, or a publicly confirmed Iran-Oman bilateral shipping arrangement, will be announced within 30 days despite this week's postponement.
forecasts.note: No reschedule date or publicly confirmed Iran-Oman bilateral arrangement identified. The diplomatic centre of gravity has shifted to UNGA, where the 22 Sep Trump-Gulf-leaders meeting and a possible Trump-Pezeshkian contact now overshadow the Salalah track. Window closes ~14 Oct.

forecasts.forecast: At least one U.S. defense-industrial-base or federal-contractor victim of the Cisco FMC exploitation (the Sandworm-linked or Qilin clusters) will be publicly confirmed within 30 days.
forecasts.note: No DIB victim named across the gap. Related evidence surfaced on an adjacent CVE: Cisco confirmed it discovered the ISE flaw while resolving a customer TAC support case, so at least one enterprise was compromised pre-disclosure, but the organization is unnamed. Tracked on the Actively Exploited Edge / DevOps / Identity / AI-Infra CVEs thread.

forecasts.forecast: The 24 Sep Trump-Xi summit will produce at least a limited, publicly announced trade/rare-earth gesture (e.g., a licensing carve-out or tariff pause) rather than no agreement or a full rupture.
forecasts.note: The summit was held 24 Sep and Treasury Secretary Bessent confirmed the US-China tariff truce is extended to 10 Jan 2027, satisfying the forecast's 'tariff pause' clause. No rare-earth-specific gesture was identified, but the forecast required only one of the two. Tracked on the China-Taiwan Pressure / Trump-Xi Summit thread.

forecasts.forecast: Formal attribution (a named actor or state sponsor) for the 10-11 Sep Petroline pipeline strike will remain unestablished for at least 14 days from the attack (through ~24-25 Sep), even as circumstantial attribution continues to firm.
forecasts.note: No formal attribution was identified within the 14-day window (through ~24-25 Sep); the strike remains formally unclaimed/unattributed. Tracked on the U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz thread.

forecasts.forecast: A confirmed downstream compromise or intrusion attributable to secrets/credentials exfiltrated via the GitLab CVE-2026-85706 exploitation will be publicly reported within 30 days.
forecasts.note: No downstream-compromise reporting tied to the GitLab exfiltration across the gap. A structurally similar incident did surface separately -- CrowdSec disclosed roughly 170 private GitHub repositories copied after a former employee's account was compromised via the May TanStack npm supply-chain attack -- but it is a different origin and does not resolve this forecast.

forecasts.forecast: DoD will publicly release its first overarching cyber strategy since 2023 within 30 days, despite having already missed its informal early-September expectation.
forecasts.note: Still unreleased into a fourth cycle. Previews sharpened this cycle to include contractor support for offensive cyber operations, a reported break from past policy. Window closes ~15 Oct. Tracked on the DoD Leadership Continuity thread.

forecasts.forecast: At least one public DoD software-related solicitation or RFP will explicitly reference Project Gatekeeper or the Accelerated Mission Software instruction within 90 days.
forecasts.note: No solicitation referencing Project Gatekeeper or the Accelerated Mission Software instruction identified. DIU's separate PROJ00716 AI sensor-fusion solicitation reaches its 24 Sep deadline this week. Tracked on the Pentagon AI-Assisted Software Acquisition thread.

forecasts.forecast: U.S. officials will provide additional public detail on the type (kinetic vs. non-kinetic) or scale of the Space Force's disclosed on-orbit space-control weapons within 90 days.
forecasts.note: No new U.S. technical detail on capability type or scale across the gap, and no adversary counter-space test. The substantive movement was in supporting architecture instead -- the 18 Sep GHOST-R GEO reconnaissance prototype awards. Tracked on the Space Control / Orbital Weapons Disclosure thread.

forecasts.forecast: A specific, publicly reported exit-ban enforcement case under China's new exit-control regulation (rare earths/batteries/semiconductors) will surface within 60 days.
forecasts.note: Still no publicly reported exit-ban enforcement case under Decree No. 841. A different restrictive mechanism became visible instead: Chinese suppliers reportedly refusing U.S.-bound shipments despite valid licences, which achieves a comparable effect with no enforcement action and therefore may reduce the need for a visible exit-ban case at all.

forecasts.forecast: Ukraine and Russia will not achieve a durable, mutually verified halt on energy-infrastructure strikes within 30 days, despite Trump's push for one.
forecasts.note: Trending strongly toward CORRECT. Ukraine's largest strike package of the war damaged a Moscow refinery facility on 19-20 Sep with no halt agreed, and United Russia's two-thirds constitutional majority removes the last internal route to a policy change. The 30-day window remains open to 16 Oct, so not graded yet.

forecasts.forecast: Following CENTCOM's reported destruction of two IRGC boats (15 Sep) -- the first acknowledged U.S. kinetic action since 8 Sep -- Iran or an aligned group (e.g., the Houthis) will conduct at least one further attempted retaliatory strike against a U.S.-linked vessel, asset, or partner (e.g., Saudi/Gulf energy infrastructure) within 14 days.
forecasts.note: Upgraded from PARTIAL to CORRECT. The 19 Sep Houthi ballistic-missile and drone attack on Riyadh and on Aramco facilities at Yanbu resolves this cleanly: Saudi Arabia itself confirmed the attempted ballistic-missile attack on its capital -- an independently established attempted retaliatory strike against a named U.S. partner, well inside the 14-day window. Unlike the earlier Iranian claims this forecast previously rested on, this one does not depend on interested-party assertion. Tracked on the U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz thread.

forecasts.forecast: The pending $14B Taiwan arms-sale package will NOT be approved by the U.S. before the 24 Sep Xi-Trump summit, and the summit will proceed as scheduled rather than be cancelled or materially downgraded.
forecasts.note: The summit proceeded as scheduled at the White House on 24 Sep with no cancellation or downgrade, and no approval of the $14B Taiwan package before or during the summit has been identified. Tracked on the China-Taiwan Pressure / Trump-Xi Summit thread.

forecasts.forecast: A confirmed enterprise or DIB-sector intrusion attributable to the newly KEV-listed Cisco ISE (CVE-2026-76460) or Secure Email Gateway (CVE-2026-76461) vulnerabilities will be publicly reported within 30 days.
forecasts.note: Partial supporting evidence surfaced: Cisco confirmed it found CVE-2026-76460 while resolving a customer TAC support case, meaning at least one enterprise was compromised before disclosure -- but no victim has been named, which is what this forecast requires. The 19 Sep federal remediation deadline has now passed and patches span 3.1 Patch 12 to 3.5 Patch 4.

forecasts.forecast: Trump will not order a major overt military action beyond the current strike posture against Iran within 30 days, despite the 'annihilate' framing in his 17 Sep Axios interview.
forecasts.note: Trending toward CORRECT: Trump rejected Iran's roadmap on 26 Sep but WSJ reports he is weighing strikes specifically after the midterms (post-~4 Nov), consistent with no major action inside this forecast's ~18 Oct window. No new major overt action confirmed yet.

forecasts.forecast: The FAR Overhaul proposed rule for Parts 9/27/47 (Federal Register 2026-19159) will proceed to a final rule within 12 months without material reversal, consistent with the broader 12-rule overhaul package under EO 14275.
forecasts.note: Context materially corrected this cycle: the 18 Sep publication comprised four proposed rules (2026-19158, -19159, -19160, -19162), and four earlier rules published 23 Jun 2026, bringing eight of twelve public. Countervailing signal to note -- final rules from the June batch reportedly stalled earlier in 2026 while OMB weighed changes, so proposed-stage publication does not guarantee timely finalization.

forecasts.forecast: Space Force's review of ULA Vulcan's Amazon Leo commercial missions will conclude without blocking Vulcan's return to national-security launches within 60 days.
forecasts.note: No public update identified during 18-21 Sep. This is an absence of reporting, not evidence that the review has concluded. Window closes ~17 Nov.

forecasts.forecast: The 24 Sep Trump-Xi summit will be held as scheduled and produce a publicly announced extension or rollover of the tariff/trade truce, but no rare-earth licensing carve-out covering military-affiliated U.S. firms.
forecasts.note: The summit was held as scheduled on 24 Sep; Treasury Secretary Bessent confirmed the tariff truce is extended to 10 Jan 2027, and no rare-earth licensing carve-out for military-affiliated firms has been identified in the readout, consistent with China's own suspension not expiring until ~10 Nov. Tracked on the China-Taiwan Pressure / Trump-Xi Summit and Critical Minerals / Rare-Earth Magnets threads.

forecasts.forecast: No publicly announced U.S.-Iran ceasefire or framework agreement will be reached within 14 days of the 22 Sep Trump-Gulf-leaders meeting, despite Pezeshkian's UNGA attendance and Trump's stated openness to meeting him.
forecasts.note: Still no framework announced as of 24 Sep, consistent with the base case. Reporting since has clarified that the 22 Sep session was conducted indirectly through Qatari intermediaries rather than face-to-face, and Araghchi faces domestic Iranian backlash -- both cut against a fast framework and restore confidence toward the original base case. Tracked on the U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz thread.

forecasts.forecast: Following the 19 Sep Houthi ballistic-missile and drone attack on Riyadh and Aramco facilities at Yanbu, at least one further Houthi strike or attempted strike on Saudi territory will be publicly reported within 21 days.
forecasts.note: Saudi coalition intercepted 2 Houthi ballistic missiles and 2 drones headed toward Riyadh/Khamis Mushait on 26 Sep -- an independently reported attempted strike well within the 21-day window (deadline ~12 Oct). Tracked on the U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz thread.

forecasts.forecast: The remaining four proposed rules needed to complete the twelve-rule Revolutionary FAR Overhaul package will be published in the Federal Register within 120 days.
forecasts.note: Eight of twelve are now public: four on 23 Jun 2026 and four on 18 Sep 2026. The roughly three-month interval between batches supports a third batch by year-end, but reporting that June-batch final rules stalled while OMB weighed changes is a countervailing signal. Tracked on the FAR Overhaul / Acquisition Reform thread.

forecasts.forecast: No confirmed U.S. defense-industrial-base or federal-contractor intrusion will be publicly attributed to the three Linux kernel KEV entries (CVE-2025-39682, CVE-2025-39964, CVE-2026-53266) within 60 days, because all three are local-privilege-escalation rather than initial-access vectors.
forecasts.note: A deliberate test of this cycle's central cyber judgment -- that the exploited class has moved to the escalation half of the intrusion chain. That underlying judgment was itself reversed on 22 Sep by two new network-facing KEV entries (Zyxel GS1900, Exchange zero-click RCE), though this forecast's specific test (a Linux-kernel-attributed victim) is unaffected since the new CVEs are a different class. If a named DIB victim is attributed to one of these kernel flaws it would more likely appear as part of a chained campaign from an edge CVE. Tracked on the Actively Exploited Edge / DevOps / Identity / AI-Infra CVEs thread.

forecasts.forecast: Following the 21-22 Sep KEV additions of CVE-2026-7273 (Zyxel GS1900) and CVE-2026-55007 (Exchange zero-click RCE), at least one further edge/perimeter/remote-access KEV addition (as opposed to a local-privilege-escalation CVE) will occur within 14 days, confirming that the 21 Sep de-escalation call was a temporary pause rather than a genuine trend.
forecasts.note: CISA's 22 Sep KEV additions -- Check Point Security Gateway/Spark pre-auth RCE (CVE-2026-85102), Check Point management pre-auth (CVE-2026-93616), Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator (CVE-2026-93952), and F5 BIG-IP APM (CVE-2026-94127, CVSS 9.8) -- are all network-facing, low-/no-interaction edge/identity-infrastructure vectors, confirming the reversal is a sustained multi-vendor trend rather than a one-off. Tracked on the Actively Exploited Edge / DevOps / Identity / AI-Infra CVEs thread.

forecasts.forecast: Saudi Aramco will publicly confirm at least a partial (roughly half-capacity) restart of the Petroline East-West pipeline within 7 days, consistent with 16 Sep guidance and prediction-market pricing (~84.5% by 30 Sep).
forecasts.note: Confirmed within 24 hours via industry-sourced reporting (Reuters/Bloomberg/FT): Aramco achieved a partial restart targeting ~4M bpd against the 7M bpd nameplate, with an export loading already scheduled at Yanbu; full capacity remains up to six weeks out pending repair of three damaged pumping stations. Graded on industry sourcing rather than a formal Aramco press statement, which has not yet been issued. Tracked on the U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz thread.

forecasts.forecast: No specific, publicly announced U.S. security-guarantee or air-defense-resupply commitment to Gulf Cooperation Council states will be identified within 14 days of the 22 Sep Trump-Gulf-leaders meeting, consistent with the postwar plan's reported deferral until after the November midterms.
forecasts.note: No specific security-guarantee or resupply commitment identified as of 23 Sep, consistent with the base case so far; reporting instead describes Gulf states independently accelerating their own layered air-defense procurement (Patriot/THAAD/counter-UAS) rather than a new US commitment. Tracked on the U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz thread.

forecasts.forecast: Following the 22 Sep Witkoff/Kushner-Araghchi three-hour session ('a lot of momentum'), a follow-on US-Iran meeting will occur within 14 days, but a publicly announced comprehensive framework covering blockade lift, asset unfreeze, and war termination will NOT be finalized within that window.
forecasts.note: Iran's written 60-day ceasefire roadmap, made public today, is a substantive escalation from the 22-23 Sep session already covered by this forecast, but is not itself a distinct 'further meeting' nor a finalized comprehensive framework -- both clauses remain open within the 14-day window. Tracked on the U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz thread.

forecasts.forecast: UN-reported displacement figures from the Houthi Red Sea coast offensive and the resulting Saudi air campaign will exceed 150,000 within 30 days, consistent with the UN's own trajectory toward a 230,000 forecast.
forecasts.note: Still tracking below the 150,000 threshold as of this cycle (last confirmed figure past 130,000, 25 Sep); the Houthi-Saudi air campaign and Yemen displacement continue widening independent of the Hormuz-focused diplomatic channel. Tracked on the U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz thread.

forecasts.forecast: Given F5 BIG-IP APM CVE-2026-94127's CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated RCE and confirmed exploitation, at least one additional vendor advisory, researcher report, or confirmed victim organization tied to this CVE will be publicly reported within 21 days.
forecasts.note: Tests whether the F5 BIG-IP APM zero-day's exploitation scope becomes more visible beyond F5's own internal-discovery disclosure. Tracked on the Actively Exploited Edge / DevOps / Identity / AI-Infra CVEs thread.

forecasts.forecast: Given Araghchi's domestic Iranian backlash and the correction that the 22 Sep session was indirect/Qatar-mediated, no further Iran-US session (direct or indirect) will be confirmed within 14 days.
forecasts.note: Iran's written roadmap was made public today, but this is disclosure of the same 22-23 Sep engagement, not a new confirmed session. No distinct further Iran-US session has been confirmed yet within the window. Tracked on the U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz thread.

forecasts.forecast: No formal Xi-Trump joint statement or fact sheet containing rare-earth licensing language for military-affiliated U.S. firms will be identified within 14 days of the 24 Sep summit.
forecasts.note: Four days into the window, still no formal joint statement or fact sheet has surfaced with rare-earth licensing language, consistent with the base case. Tracked on the Critical Minerals / Rare-Earth Magnets and China-Taiwan Pressure / Trump-Xi Summit threads.

forecasts.forecast: DoD will complete (or credible reporting will confirm) 100% migration off classified Anthropic workloads by the 29 Sep department-wide deadline, absent a new D.C. Circuit ruling or injunction in the interim.
forecasts.note: A new DC Circuit ruling did occur (25 Sep) but it upheld rather than blocked the designation, reinforcing rather than disrupting the migration timeline. Deadline is tomorrow; DoD reported ~90% migrated as of mid-September. Tracked on the DoD AI Vendor Governance / Anthropic Dispute thread.

forecasts.forecast: No formal U.S. public acceptance or rejection of Iran's written 60-day ceasefire roadmap will be issued within 14 days, given the need to weigh explicit Israeli objections and reported midterm-timing pressure.
forecasts.note: Trump publicly rejected the roadmap (now detailed as a seven-day Hormuz-reopening plan) on 26 Sep, calling its terms unacceptable -- a formal rejection within roughly 24 hours, well inside the 14-day window this forecast bet against. Tracked on the U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz thread.

forecasts.forecast: At least one confirmed enterprise or DIB-sector victim organization (beyond F5's own internal discovery) tied to CVE-2026-94127 will be publicly reported within 21 days of today's federal remediation deadline.
forecasts.note: Tests whether the F5 BIG-IP APM zero-day's exploitation scope becomes visible beyond F5's own vendor-discovered case. Tracked on the Actively Exploited Edge / DevOps / Identity / AI-Infra CVEs thread.

forecasts.forecast: Following WSJ reporting that Trump is weighing renewed strikes on Iran after the November midterms, at least one U.S. or Israeli kinetic action against Iran (beyond the current blockade/skirmish posture) will occur within 90 days.
forecasts.note: Tests whether the reported post-midterm strike option becomes an actual decision. Tracked on the U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz thread.

forecasts.forecast: Anthropic will formally petition for en banc rehearing or seek Supreme Court review of the DC Circuit's 25 Sep 2-1 ruling within 30 days.
forecasts.note: The ruling's own 7-day stay (the practical window to preserve the status quo pending review) lapsed ~10/2 with no confirmed filing located; the broader 30-day forecast window remains open to ~10/28. As of 10/6, still no filing found, and the deadline itself is now revealed as ambiguous across secondary sources (7-day stay vs. a separately described 14-day en banc window to ~10/9) -- needs direct docket verification. Tracked on the DoD/Federal AI Governance & Vendor Policy thread.

forecasts.forecast: At least one confirmed enterprise or DIB-sector victim organization tied to the Citrix NetScaler zero-days (CVE-2026-88771/CVE-2026-88772) will be publicly reported within 30 days, given confirmed multi-week pre-patch exploitation including webshell deployment.
forecasts.note: Tests whether the confirmed pre-patch zero-day exploitation window produced a discoverable named victim, given the unusually long undisclosed-exploitation period. Tracked on the Actively Exploited Edge / DevOps / Identity / AI-Infra CVEs thread.

forecasts.forecast: The U.S. will issue some public response (accept, reject, or counter) to Iran's revised Qatar-mediated Hormuz-reopening proposal within 7 days (by ~6 Oct 2026).
forecasts.note: Iran's government spokeswoman confirmed on 30 Sep that Araghchi presented President Pezeshkian with the official U.S. response, delivered via Qatari mediators -- one day after the forecast was made and well within the 7-day window. The response's content was not disclosed, but the forecast's specific test (that some response would be issued) is met. Tracked on the U.S.-Iran Conflict / Strait of Hormuz thread.

forecasts.forecast: DoD or an independent investigation will publicly attribute the DMDC breach to either a criminal or a nation-state actor within 30 days.
forecasts.note: As of disclosure (29 Sep), no attribution has been made public despite a nine-month undetected dwell time. Tracked on the Pentagon DMDC Personnel Data Breach thread.

forecasts.forecast: The 29 Sep SASC hearing testimony will not resolve the ~$185B-vs-~$1.2T Golden Dome cost dispute, and DoD will continue to decline a full CBO methodology briefing, within 30 days.
forecasts.note: Tests whether today's hearing produces a reconciled cost baseline or DoD-CBO cooperation, given DoD's reported prior refusals of CBO briefing requests. Tracked on the Golden Dome Procurement thread.
